$comment: unity-game-factory's task format, GameTask (game-task/1, Unity flavour: Unity 6.3 LTS, metres, Y up): one task a game ships with, on its orphan tasks branch (Tasks/<name>.json) and, split into the agent's and the grader's parts, in its dataset. The deterministic `probe` check kind is described for task authors in docs/task-probes.md, and every task is seeded; a build check's `fails_at_start` marks a start that doesn't compile. tools/validate-game.py checks every task in a game repo's tasks branch and in a dataset against this schema and the rules it cannot express.

ActionsJudge.description:
A reviewer's question over what the agent did, from its own trace: each tool call in order (the tool, its
arguments and what it returned, cut), whether it worked, and which made a checkpoint; never the agent's reasoning
or messages. How the game was made counts beside the game itself (the owner, 2026-10-14: grade "based on agent
actions, and the final build").
ActionsJudge.title: ActionsJudge

AssetMeasure.description:
The project as saved, read in one batchmode editor pass: an asset (`asset`, its path) with `prop:<path>` (reflection on the
main asset, else a SerializedObject property path), `import:<path>` (its importer's), `shader:<Property>` (a
material's shader property: a float, `.r|g|b|a` of a colour, 1 when a texture is set) or `keyword:<NAME>` (1 when
the material enables it); or objects of a scene (`scene`) or a prefab (`prefab`) that `select` matches, with
`count`, `material_default` (1 when any renderer's slot is empty, missing or Unity's default material),
`material:<property>`, `mesh_collision` (1 when a mesh object has a collider) or `prop:<Component>.<path>`.
AssetMeasure.title: AssetMeasure

AtCamera.description: The player camera (Camera.main), `forward` m along its view.
AtCamera.title: AtCamera

AtXYZ.description: A fixed point in the world (m, Y up).
AtXYZ.title: AtXYZ

AudioMeasure.description:
What the player hears (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.16): the AudioSources playing that `select` matches, each at its volume at the
listener (its volume, 0 when muted, times its distance attenuation by its rolloff, its 3D share by spatialBlend;
mixer volumes and AudioListener.volume left out): `count` (how many), `audible` (how many at 0.001, -60 dB, or
louder), `volume` (their sum), `max_volume` (the loudest); `level` (the RMS of the listener's mixed output since
the previous sample, mixers and effects included). A play with an audio measure runs paced to real time with its
sound measured and silenced. The volumes' and the level's threshold is calibrated or relative to the start,
never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
AudioMeasure.title: AudioMeasure

AudioSelect.description:
The AudioSources playing (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.16): by their AudioClip's name (`sound`, a wildcard), their output
AudioMixerGroup's name (`sound_class`, a wildcard), and an owner object the `owner` select matches (the source on
it or its descendants); none: every source playing.
AudioSelect.title: AudioSelect

Axis.description:
An axis control set to a value (<Mouse>/delta/x, <Gamepad>/leftStick/x), e.g. mouse look: <Mouse>/delta/* and
<Mouse>/scroll/* are one-frame impulses; any other axis keeps its value until set again.
Axis.title: Axis

Boot.description:
The game starts (the built player, windowed 960x540, its window moved off-screen) and runs `seconds` with no crash and
no fatal error in its player log.
Boot.title: Boot

Build.description:
The scripts compile and a Windows player builds (x64, Mono, non-development, of the scratch copy). `fails_at_start`:
the task's start doesn't build, and making it build is the task (a compile error Unity rejects); the start is never
played, so nothing in the task may need it played (docs/task-probes.md, section 3.1; tools/validate-game.py).
Build.title: Build

Calibrate.description: Threshold s + f * (r - s): the start (s) and the developers' fix (r) measured in the grading environment.
Calibrate.title: Calibrate

CameraMeasure.description:
The player camera (Camera.main, else the enabled camera of highest depth that renders to the screen): `distance`
(m to the player), `height` (its y minus the player's), `pitch` (positive looks down), `yaw` (degrees, as the
Inspector shows them), `fov` (vertical, degrees; 0 for an orthographic camera), `occluded` (a collider that isn't
the player's lies between the camera and the player's centre), `player_on_screen` (the player's centre projects
inside the viewport, in front).
CameraMeasure.title: CameraMeasure

Click.description:
A click on the first visible, interactable uGUI Selectable or UI Toolkit Button whose name (a wildcard) or type
matches, as a player's click fires it.
Click.title: Click

CodeJudge.description:
A code reviewer's question over the run's own change (its diff from the start, text files) beside the game's
real change for the same problem (the seed's `reference`, a bug's fix from the game's history), which the agent
never sees.
CodeJudge.title: CodeJudge

ComponentSelect.description:
Components of a C# type (`component`: ParticleSystem, DecalProjector, AudioSource, Light, a game's own MonoBehaviour;
base types and interfaces match), optionally on an object the `owner` select matches (or its descendants), by
its object's name (`name`, a wildcard), near a point, of a mesh renderer's mesh (`mesh`, a wildcard), and
`visible`: only the components drawn (as the `visible` field reads them); `effect`: only live effects, whatever
made them (a ParticleSystem playing or holding particles, a VisualEffect holding particles, an enabled
DecalProjector, a TrailRenderer drawing points), with or without `component` (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5).

inactive.title: Inactive
inactive.description: true: components of objects that are not active in the hierarchy match too (default: only those of active objects).

ComponentSelect.title: ComponentSelect

ComponentsMeasure.description:
Components (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5): `active` (enabled and active in the hierarchy; a ParticleSystem also playing or
holding particles; an AudioSource playing); `visible` (a Renderer enabled, active and not forced off; any other
component: its object is active); `x`, `y`, `z` and `speed` (m/s) and `spin` (deg/s) of its transform;
`extent_x|y|z` (a Renderer's or Collider's world bounds' half-size, m) and `simulating`; `intensity` and `on`
(enabled, active, an intensity above 0) of a Light; `changed` (1 when a Renderer differs from the first sample it
was seen in: hidden or shown, its world bounds moved, a skinned mesh's pose moved), `bounds_change` and
`pose_change` (m, the amounts behind it); `lit` (1 when it gives off light: a Light that is on, or a drawn mesh
whose material is emissive or unlit and bright, read from its properties where its shader has the standard
interface and else as rendered) and `glow` (how much, one amount over every kind of source, particle systems
among them; docs/task-probes.md, sections 2.4 and 2.5), the way to check for light whatever a build made it with;
`prop:<path>` (a field or property of the component by reflection; strings through `match`). `intensity`,
`extent_*`, `bounds_change`, `pose_change`, `glow` and `spin` depend on what a build chose, so their threshold is
calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
ComponentsMeasure.title: ComponentsMeasure

Cursor.description:
The virtual mouse moved to a viewport point (fractions 0-1, y down from the top); a following <Mouse>/leftButton
press clicks there.
Cursor.title: Cursor

DrawnMeasure.description:
What is drawn in a place, whatever draws it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.19): every renderer drawn whose bounds reach the place
(`near` a point, its height band applied; or within `radius` of a `line`), rendered alone from fixed orthographic
views, each pixel kept where its depth puts it inside the place. Near a point: `drawn` (1 when anything is),
`motion` (the share of what is drawn there that changed since the previous sample: a moving mesh, particles, a
scrolled material), `base_r|g|b` (the mean surface colour, rendered under flat white ambient light with no direct
lights, fog or post-processing, linear 0-1) and `base_change` (that colour's distance from the first sample's).
Along a line: `drawn`, `reach` (m from `from` to the furthest point drawn on it) and `length` (m of it drawn).
Every field but `drawn` depends on what a build drew, so its threshold is calibrated or relative to the start,
never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
DrawnMeasure.title: DrawnMeasure

FileExists.description: At least `min_count` project files match `glob` (relative to the project; e.g. Assets/Scenes/*.unity).
FileExists.title: FileExists

GradingMeasure.description:
The colour pipeline (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.8): a neutral grey lit by the key light and run through URP's colour grading as
the volume stack at the camera sets it: `grey`, `cast`, `warmth`, `tint`, `saturation`, `contrast`; or a volume
parameter after blending, `post:<Component>.<parameter>` (post:Bloom.intensity, post:ColorAdjustments.postExposure).
GradingMeasure.title: GradingMeasure

GroundMeasure.description:
The ground (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.17): where a ray straight down from 2000 m up meets a collider first (triggers and the
player's aside; with `select`, only colliders of objects it matches count), at a point `xz` [x, z] (`height`, y in
m; `hit`, 1 when it met anything) or over a box `box` [x0, z0, x1, z1] sampled on a `grid` x `grid` lattice
(`min`, `max`, `mean` of the heights, `range` = max - min, the relief; `hits`). `range`'s threshold is calibrated
or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
GroundMeasure.title: GroundMeasure

Has.description:
A component the object carries (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4): it matches when one of its parts (the components of
itself and its descendants) matches every key given: `component` (its C# type, a base type or an interface, by
name or full name), `lit` (it gives off light, as the components `lit` field reads it), `visible` (drawn, as
the components `visible` field reads it), `near` (the part's own place within `radius` m of a point),
`simulating` (a non-kinematic Rigidbody or a Dynamic Rigidbody2D), `movable` (not static: a transform a player can
shove).
Has.title: Has

Judge.description:
The game judge's question over evidence the grader takes itself (screenshots and gameplay frames of a scripted
play, and the brief), item by item; never the agent's own words. `before`: the grader also plays the game as it
was at the start, and the judge compares (a seeded task that changes how the game looks or plays). `route`: a
project file in which the agent leaves inputs that play its game through (the probe's [{t, key, press}] with Input System
control paths, e.g. Tests/win_route.json); the grader plays it in its own clean copy as one more play, and the judge is told when
the file is missing or isn't a route.
Judge.title: Judge

Key.description:
A control pressed or released on the probe's virtual devices: an Input System control path on <Keyboard>,
<Mouse> or <Gamepad> (<Keyboard>/w, <Keyboard>/space, <Mouse>/leftButton, <Gamepad>/buttonSouth).
Key.title: Key

LightMeasure.description:
Light reaching a point, as URP computes it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.7): `illuminance` (the lights that are on, each by its
intensity, colour, distance and cone attenuation and a visibility test, plus the ambient), `exposure` (2^postExposure
of the volume stack at the camera), `brightness` (illuminance x exposure).
LightMeasure.title: LightMeasure

Line.description: A segment from `from` to `to` (points), and how far from it (`radius`, m) counts as on it.
Line.title: Line

LogAbsent.description: No line of the game's log during a boot matches `pattern` (a regular expression).
LogAbsent.title: LogAbsent

LogMeasure.description: Lines of the play's player log matching `pattern`.
LogMeasure.title: LogMeasure

Near.description:
Within `radius` m of `point`; `y_min`/`y_max` (m) also keep it within a height band: world y, or offsets from
the point's y with `y_relative` (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.13).
Near.title: Near

ObjectsMeasure.description:
GameObjects (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4): `count`; `x`, `y`, `z` (m, Y up); `yaw`, `pitch`, `roll` (euler Y, X, Z, as the
Inspector shows them, in (-180, 180]); `scale` (mean of |lossyScale|); `extent_x|y|z` (m, the world-aligned
half-size of its drawn renderers' bounds, descendants included); `active` (activeInHierarchy); `hidden` (inactive,
or none of its renderers drawn); `collision` (an enabled non-trigger collider); `speed` (m/s); `spin` (deg/s);
`simulating` (a non-kinematic Rigidbody or a Dynamic Rigidbody2D); `spread` (m, the diagonal of the box around its
drawn renderers' centres); `changed`, `bounds_change`, `pose_change` (m) against the first sample it was seen in;
`lit` and `glow` (as the components fields, over its parts); `prop:<Component>.<member>[.<sub>]` (a field or
property by reflection; `prop:<member>` alone reads the GameObject, else its Transform; strings through `match`);
`bone:<Component>.<Bone>.x|y|z`; `rel_yaw:<Part>`, `world_yaw:`/`world_pitch:`/`world_roll:<Part>`,
`forward:<Part>.x|y|z` (a Part is a descendant by name, else the first object in it carrying a component of that
type); `facing_vs_velocity` (degrees); `anim:<Parameter>` (its Animator's parameter); `clip` (its Animator's
current clip on layer 0, through `match`). `spin`, `spread`, `bounds_change`, `pose_change` and `glow` depend
on what a build chose, so their threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal
(tools/validate-game.py).
ObjectsMeasure.title: ObjectsMeasure

Package.description:
A Windows player builds from the project's own build settings (its enabled build scenes, as a release would), and
the built player boots.
Package.title: Package

PieceSelect.description:
Drawn mesh pieces (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): of renderers of a C# type (MeshRenderer, SkinnedMeshRenderer, Terrain for its
tree instances; default every one), optionally by their object's name, their mesh's name (`mesh`, a
wildcard), an owner object the `owner` select matches, and near a point (each piece by its own place).
PieceSelect.title: PieceSelect

PiecesMeasure.description:
Drawn mesh pieces, whatever their form (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): a MeshRenderer with a mesh that has triangles is one, a
SkinnedMeshRenderer one, a Terrain's tree instances one each; under a LODGroup only LOD 0's renderers count;
counted over all of them, never cut at the rows cap. `components` (renderers), `objects` (their objects).
`triangles`/`visible_triangles`: the triangles those pieces (those drawn) hold (index count / 3 over their
submeshes); they depend on the meshes a build chose, so their threshold is calibrated or relative to the start,
never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
PiecesMeasure.title: PiecesMeasure

PlayerMeasure.title: PlayerMeasure

Probe.description:
A deterministic check (docs/task-probes.md): `measure` taken where `play` says, reduced to one number, compared with
`expect`. `describe` is the assertion in plain English, shown in the grade.
Probe.title: Probe

ScreenMeasure.description:
The frame the player sees (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.15): mean luminance of the frame as displayed, UI included (keep the rect
off the HUD), over `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in viewport fractions, y down (default the whole frame). It moves
between machines, so its threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
ScreenMeasure.title: ScreenMeasure

Seed.description:
Where a seeded task starts: one of the studio's Unity games at `commit`. `game` is its slug: the game's repository
(unity-game-<slug>) and its folder under the machine's games root. Both commits are Unity 6000.3 projects as
committed (ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt; tools/validate-game.py).
`reference`: a later commit of that game whose change solves the task (a bug's fix), for calibrated probes, the code judge and the task check.
`history`: which history the two commits are from: "private", the game's own repository (its clone,
GitHub, a mirror), or "dataset", the rewritten history a Dataset.zip delivers (History/), whose
commit ids differ; the game's commit map translates either way.
Seed.title: Seed

Select.description:
GameObjects that match every key given: `component` (a component it carries, by C# type name or full name; base
types and interfaces match), `tag` (its tag), `layer` (its layer, by name), `name` (a wildcard on its name),
`near` (within `radius` m of a point), `player` (the player object), `has` (a part it carries that matches
every key given there: an object that gives light, one with a drawn mesh near a point), `inactive` (inactive
objects match too; without it only objects active in the hierarchy do).
Select.title: Select

SpawnsMeasure.description:
Objects carrying the component (a C# type) that appeared (became active) or went, counted every frame since the play
started (cumulative; the checker differences them).
SpawnsMeasure.title: SpawnsMeasure

StartPlus.description: Threshold s + d: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartPlus.title: StartPlus

StartTimes.description: Threshold s * f: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartTimes.title: StartTimes

TaskPlay.description:
A task-defined scripted play: `inputs` (controls, axes, widget clicks, cursor moves, teleports, waits) sent at their times
during `seconds`, and samples every `every` seconds (default 0.5). `scene` and `args`, when the key is present,
take the place of the task's play_scene and play_args for this play (null: the project's first build scene;
[]: no arguments). Arguments are the player's command line (a flag, -name, then its values), never the grader's
own: -batchmode, -nographics, -quit, -logFile, -projectPath, -executeMethod, -popupwindow, -monitor,
-parentHWND, -single-instance, -screen-*, -force-*, -taskProbe* (docs/task-probes.md section 1.1; tools/validate-game.py).
TaskPlay.title: TaskPlay

Teleport.description:
The player placed at `teleport` (m) facing `yaw` (degrees about Y): the grader's own way to reach a test spot; `hold`:
for that many seconds of play the player is put back there after every frame's game logic, for a game that sets
its player's place every frame (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Teleport.title: Teleport

TeleportTo.description:
The player placed next to the object `teleport_to` selects nearest to it (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1): `distance` m from
it on the player's side, level with it, plus `offset` (m), facing `face` (a point) or else that object; for a spot
a build chose itself (an ore it placed). Nothing happens when no object matches. `hold`: as a teleport's, the
player kept at that spot for that many seconds of play (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
TeleportTo.title: TeleportTo

TraceMeasure.description: A fact of the agent's own trace (never gating).
TraceMeasure.title: TraceMeasure

UiMeasure.description:
What the UI shows on screen, whatever draws it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): the elements on screen in the frame drawn right
after each sample, from uGUI graphics on screen-space canvases (Text, TMP_Text, Image, RawImage and any other
drawn graphic) and UI Toolkit elements alike, only what is drawn (an inactive, disabled, transparent, hidden or
undisplayed element is not; world-space canvases and 3D text are not UI). `count` (one per element), `text` (with
`match`; a select of text with a `rect` also reads the frame as drawn there, however the text was drawn: OnGUI,
GL, a custom mesh), `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` (its rectangle in viewport fractions, y down); `of` combines the elements
`select` picks. `signature`: one value a sample for everything the select picks (kinds, texts, rectangles), read
with `agg` `changes` (how many samples show something other than the one before: a readout that updates,
however it is drawn), `any`, `all` or `count` (samples showing anything); `of` is ignored (docs/task-probes.md,
section 2.18). `number`: the first number its text elements show, in reading order; `clock`: the first time they
show (h:mm:ss, m:ss, or else a number, as seconds); read with `rises`, `falls`, `changes` or `range` for which
way it moved, `of` ignored (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18). The way to check what a HUD shows, however a build
drew it.
UiMeasure.title: UiMeasure

UiSelect.description:
Which of the UI elements on screen (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): `kind` (text, box, image), `text` (a regular expression
the element's text must match; text elements only) and `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in viewport fractions, y down
from the top (the element's centre inside); none: every element on screen.
UiSelect.title: UiSelect

Value.description: A literal threshold, for facts that don't depend on the scene (counts, booleans).
Value.title: Value

Wait.description:
At `t` the play's clock holds for `wait` seconds of real time while the game runs on, paced to real time (each
frame waits for the wall clock to catch up with the game's own time), for what runs on the wall clock (a menu that
pages on real time). No samples, inputs or screenshots meanwhile; then the play goes on from `t` (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Wait.title: Wait

WidgetSelect.description:
Widgets: uGUI components (UnityEngine.UI Graphics and Selectables, TextMeshPro) on their objects and UI Toolkit
elements of every UIDocument panel, by their type (`component`: Button, Slider, TMP_Text, Label, ProgressBar, a
game's own type) and/or name (a wildcard on the object's or element's name); `text`: a regular expression the
widget's text must match; `visible`: only the widgets drawn (as the `visible` field reads them: never an
inactive, hidden or transparent one, nor one under such a parent), so a select counts what is on screen.
WidgetSelect.title: WidgetSelect

WidgetsMeasure.description:
Widgets (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.6): uGUI and UI Toolkit. `count`, `visible`, `text` (with `match`), `percent` (a Slider's
normalizedValue, a filled Image's fillAmount, a ProgressBar's share, a Scrollbar's value), `value` (a Slider's
value, a Toggle's 1/0), `interactable`, `has_brush` (a sprite, texture or background image is set), `brush` (its
name, with `match`), `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` (viewport fractions 0-1, y down from the top).
WidgetsMeasure.title: WidgetsMeasure

play_args.description:
The player's command-line arguments for every play of the task (-scenario 2: ["-scenario", "2"]); never the
grader's own flags (TaskPlay).
play_args.title: Play Args

play_scene.description: The scene every play of the task opens (null: the project's first build scene).
play_scene.title: Play Scene

player.description:
The player object for every play of the task (CameraMeasure, PlayerMeasure, `player` points and selects),
when the default finds the wrong one.

title: game-task/1
